questions.question: Electromagnetic emissions from a terminal represent a risk because they:

options.A: can damage or erase nearby storage media.
options.C: can have adverse health effects on personnel.

questions.correct_explanation: Emissions can be detected by sophisticated equipment and displayed, thus giving unauthorized persons access to data. TEMPEST is a term referring to the investigation and study of compromising emanations of unintentional intelligence-bearing signals that, if intercepted and analyzed, may reveal their contents.

wrong_explanations.A: Although a strong magnetic field can erase certain storage media, normally terminals are designed to limit these emissions; therefore, this is not normally a concern.
wrong_explanations.B: Electromagnetic emissions should not cause disruption of central processing units.
wrong_explanations.C: Most electromagnetic emissions are low level and do not pose a significant health risk.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Security administration procedures require read-only access to:
questions.correct_explanation: Security administration procedures require read-only access to security log files to ensure that, once generated, the logs are not modified. Logs provide evidence and track suspicious transactions and activities.

wrong_explanations.A: Security administration procedures require write access to access control tables to manage and update the privileges according to authorized business requirements.
wrong_explanations.C: Logging options require write access to allow the administrator to update the way the transactions and user activities are monitored, captured, stored, processed and reported.
wrong_explanations.D: The security administrator is often responsible for user-facing issues, such as managing user roles, profiles and settings. This requires the administrator to have more than read-only access.

tips: Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: With the help of a security officer, granting access to data is the responsibility of:
questions.correct_explanation: Data owners are responsible for the access to and use of data. Written authorization for users to gain access to computerized information should be provided by the data owners. Security administration with the owners' approval sets up access rules stipulating which users or group of users are authorized to access data or files and the level of authorized access (e.g., read or update).

wrong_explanations.B: Programmers develop the access control software that regulates the ways that users can access the data (update, read, delete, etc.), but the programmers do not have responsibility for determining who gets access to data.
wrong_explanations.C: Systems analysts work with the owners and programmers to design access controls according to the rules set by the owners.
wrong_explanations.D: The librarians enforce the access control procedures they have been given but do not determine who gets access.

tips: Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: The FIRST step in data classification is to:
questions.correct_explanation: Data classification is necessary to define access rules based on a need-to-do and need-to-know basis. The data owner is responsible for defining the access rules; therefore, establishing ownership is the first step in data classification.

wrong_explanations.B: A criticality analysis is required to determine the appropriate levels of protection of data, according to the data classification.
wrong_explanations.C: Access rules are set up dependent of the data classification.
wrong_explanations.D: Input for a data dictionary is prepared from the results of the data classification process.

questions.question: Which stage of a biometrics system operation should the information systems (IS) auditor review FIRST?
questions.correct_explanation: The users must first be enrolled to use a biometric device; therefore, the information systems (IS)auditor should review this stage first.

wrong_explanations.B: The device captures a physical or behavioral image of the human, identifies the unique features and uses an algorithm to convert them into a string of numbers stored as a template to be used in the matching processes.
wrong_explanations.C: A user applying for access will be verified against the stored enrolled value.
wrong_explanations.D: The biometric stores sensitive personal information, so the storage must be secure.

questions.question: A hacker can obtain passwords without the use of computer tools or programs through the technique of:
questions.correct_explanation: Social engineering is based on the divulgence of private information through dialogues, interviews, inquiries, etc., in which a user may be indiscreet regarding their or someone else's personal data.

wrong_explanations.B: A sniffer is a computer tool to monitor the traffic in networks.
wrong_explanations.C: Back doors are computer programs left by hackers to exploit vulnerabilities.
wrong_explanations.D: Trojan horses are computer programs that pretend to supplant a real program; thus, the functionality of the program is not authorized and is usually malicious in nature.

questions.question: The reliability of an application system's audit trail may be questionable if:

options.A: user IDs are recorded in the audit trail.
options.B: the security administrator has read-only rights to the audit file.
options.C: date and time stamps are recorded when an action occurs.
options.D: users can amend audit trail records when correcting system errors.

questions.correct_explanation: An audit trail is not effective if the details in it can be amended.

wrong_explanations.A: An audit trail must record the identity of the person or process involved in the logged activity to establish accountability.
wrong_explanations.B: Restricting the administrator to read-only access will protect the audit file from alteration.
wrong_explanations.C: Data and time stamps should be recorded in the logs to enable the reconstruction and correlation of events on multiple systems.

questions.question: While conducting an audit, an information systems (IS) auditor detects the presence of a virus. What should be the IS auditor's NEXT step?

options.B: Clear the virus from the network.

questions.correct_explanation: The first thing an IS auditor should do after detecting the virus is to alert the organization to its presence, then wait for their response.

wrong_explanations.A: Observing the response mechanism should be done after informing appropriate personnel. This enables an information systems (IS) auditor to examine the actual workability and effectiveness of the response system.
wrong_explanations.B: The IS auditor is neither authorized nor capable in most cases of removing the virus from the network.
wrong_explanations.D: An IS auditor should not make changes to the system being audited; ensuring the deletion of the virus is a management responsibility.

questions.question: The implementation of access controls FIRST requires:

options.A: a classification of information systems (IS) resources.
options.C: the creation of an access control list.

questions.correct_explanation: The first step in implementing access controls is an inventory of IS resources, which is the basis for establishing ownership and classification.

wrong_explanations.A: The first step in implementing access controls is an inventory of information systems (IS) resources, which is the basis for classification.
wrong_explanations.B: Labeling resources cannot be done without first determining the resources' classifications.
wrong_explanations.C: The access control list is not done without a meaningful classification of resources.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the defense in-depth security principle?

options.A: Using two firewalls to consecutively check the incoming network traffic
options.B: Using a firewall as well as logical access controls on the hosts to control incoming network traffic
options.C: Lack of physical signs on the outside of a computer center building
options.D: Using two firewalls in parallel to check different types of incoming traffic

questions.correct_explanation: Defense in-depth means using different security mechanisms that back up each other. When network traffic passes the firewall unintentionally, the logical access controls form a second line of defense.

wrong_explanations.A: Use of two firewalls does not represent an effective defense in-depth strategy because the same attack can circumvent both devices. By using two different products, the probability of both products having the same vulnerabilities is diminished.
wrong_explanations.C: Having no physical signs on the outside of a computer center building is a single security measure known as security by obscurity.
wrong_explanations.D: Using two firewalls in parallel to check different types of incoming traffic provides redundancy but is only a single security mechanism and, therefore, no different than having a single firewall checking all traffic.

tips: Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST access control procedure?

options.A: The data owner formally authorizes access and an administrator implements the user authorization tables.
options.B: Authorized staff implements the user authorization tables and the data owner approves them.
options.C: The data owner and an information systems (IS) manager jointly create and update the user authorization tables.
options.D: The data owner creates and updates the user authorization tables.

questions.correct_explanation: The data owner holds the privilege and responsibility for formally establishing the access rights. An information systems (IS) administrator should then implement or update user authorization tables at the direction of the owner.

wrong_explanations.B: The owner sets the rules and conditions for access. It is best to obtain approval before implementing the tables.
wrong_explanations.C: The data owner may consult with the IS manager to set out access control rules, but the responsibility for appropriate access remains with the data owner. The IT department should set up the access control tables at the direction of the owner.
wrong_explanations.D: The data owner does not usually manage updates to the authorization tables.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: Which of the following MOST effectively reduces social engineering incidents?
questions.correct_explanation: Social engineering exploits human nature and weaknesses to ol>taio in ormation and access privileges. By increasing employee awareness of security issues it is po ible to reduce the number of successful social engineering incidents.

wrong_explanations.B: In most cases, social engineering incidents do not require the physical presence of the intruder. Therefore, increased physical security measures would not prevent the incident.
wrong_explanations.C: An email monitoring policy informs users that all email in the organization is subject to monitoring; it does not protect the users from potential security incidents and intruders.
wrong_explanations.D: Intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are used to detect irregular or abnormal traffic patterns.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: An information security policy stating that "a fixed time duration of inactivity must initiate a password­enabled screensaver" addresses which of the following attack methods?
questions.correct_explanation: Shoulder surfing refers to observing a user while entering/viewing sensitive data on the screen. This may enable the observer to obtain login information or other sensitive information.

wrong_explanations.A: Piggybacking refers to unauthorized persons following, either physically or virtually, authorized persons into restricted areas. Initiating a screensaver that requires user to reenter the password prevents someone from tailgating an authorized person.
wrong_explanations.B: This policy only refers to the user's computer, not dumpster diving (looking through the organization's trash for valuable information).
wrong_explanations.D: Impersonation refers to someone acting as an employee in an attempt to retrieve desired information.

tips: Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: To ensure compliance with a security policy requiring that passwords be a combination of letters and numbers an information systems (IS) auditor should recommend that:

options.C: an automated password management tool be used.

questions.correct_explanation: The use of an automated password management tool is a preventive control measure. The software prevents repetition (semantic) and enforces syntactic rules, thus making the passwords robust. It also provides a method for ensuring frequent changes and prevents the same user from reusing his/her old password for a designated period of time.

wrong_explanations.A: The policy is appropriate and does not require change. Changing the policy would not ensure compliance.
wrong_explanations.B: Having a requirement to periodically change passwords is good practice and should be in the password policy.
wrong_explanations.D: Security awareness training does not enforce compliance.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.
Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviewing digital rights management applications should expect to find an extensive use for which of the following technologies?
questions.correct_explanation: Steganography is a technique for concealing the existence of messages or information within another message. An increasingly important steganographic technique is digital watermarking, which hides data within data (e.g., by encoding rights information in a picture or music file without altering the picture or music's perceivable aesthetic qualities).

wrong_explanations.A: Digitalized signatures are the scans of a signature (not the same as a digital signature) and not related to digital rights management.
wrong_explanations.B: Hashing creates a message hash or digest, which is used to ensure the integrity of the message; it is usually considered a part of cryptography.
wrong_explanations.C: Parsing is the process of splitting up a continuous stream of characters for analytical purposes and is widely applied in the design of programming languages or in data entry editing.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: The information security policy that states "each individual must have his/her badge read at every controlled door" addresses which of the following attack methods?
questions.correct_explanation: Piggybacking refers to unauthorized persons following authorized persons, either physically or virtually, into restricted areas. This policy addresses the polite behavior problem of holding doors open for a stranger. If every employee must have their badge read at every controlled door, no unauthorized person can enter the sensitive area.

wrong_explanations.B: Shoulder surfing (looking over the shoulder of a person to view sensitive information on a screen or desk) would not be prevented by the implementation of this policy.
wrong_explanations.C: Dumpster diving, looking through organization's trash for valuable information, can be done outside the enterprise's physical perimeter; therefore, this policy would not address this attack method.
wrong_explanations.D: Impersonation refers to an unauthorized person acting as an employee, trying to retrieve the desired information. Some forms of social engineering attacks can join an impersonation attack and piggybacking, but this information security policy does not address the impersonation attack.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following presents an inherent risk with no distinct identifiable preventive controls?
questions.correct_explanation: Data diddling involves changing data before they are entered into the computer. It is one of the most common abuses because it requires limited technical knowledge and occurs before computer security can protect the data. There are only compensating controls for data diddling.

wrong_explanations.A: Piggybacking is the act of following an authorized person through a secured door and can be prevented using deadman doors. Logical piggybacking is an attempt to gain access through someone who has the rights (e.g., electronically attaching to an authorized telecommunication link to possibly intercept transmissions). This can be prevented by encrypting the message.
wrong_explanations.B: Viruses are malicious program code inserted into another executable code that can self-replicate and spread from computer to computer via sharing of computer disks, transfer of logic over telecommunication lines or direct contact with an infected machine. Antivirus software can be used to protect the computer against viruses.
wrong_explanations.D: The shutdown of an application can be initiated through terminals or microcomputers connected directly (online) or indirectly (dial-up line) to the computer. Only individuals knowing the high-level logon ID and password can initiate the shutdown process, which is effective if there are proper access controls.

tips: Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: When performing a computer forensic investigation, in regard to the evidence gathered, an information systems (IS) auditor should be MOST concerned with:
questions.correct_explanation: Preservation and documentation of evidence for review by law enforcement and judicial authorities are of primary concern when investigating. Failure to properly preserve the evidence can jeopardize the admissibility of the evidence in legal proceedings.

wrong_explanations.A: Analysis is important but not the primary concern related to evidence in a forensic investigation.
wrong_explanations.B: Evaluation is important but not the primary concern related to evidence in a forensic investigation.
wrong_explanations.D: Disclosure is important but not of primary concern to the information systems (IS) auditor in a forensic investigation.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: A certificate (certification) authority (CA) can delegate the processes of:

options.A: revocation and suspension of a subscriber's certificate.
options.B: generation and distribution of the CA public key.
options.C: establishing a link between the requesting entity and its public key.

questions.correct_explanation: Establishing a link between the requesting entity and its public key is a function of a registration authority. This may or may not be performed by a CA; therefore, this function can be delegated.

wrong_explanations.A: Revocation and suspension of the subscriber certificate are functions of the subscriber certificate life cycle management, which the certificate (certification) authority (CA) must perform.
wrong_explanations.B: Generation and distribution of the CA public key is a part of the CA key life cycle management process and, as such, cannot be delegated.
wrong_explanations.D: Issuance and distribution of the subscriber certificate are functions of the subscriber certificate life cycle management, which the CA must perform.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: Which of the following results in a denial-of-service (DoS) attack?
questions.correct_explanation: The use of Ping with a packet size higher than 65 kilobyte (KB) and no fragmentation flag on will cause a denial of service.

wrong_explanations.A: A brute force attack is typically a text attack that exhausts all possible key combinations used against encryption keys or passwords.
wrong_explanations.C: A leapfrog attack, the act oftelneting through one or more hosts to preclude a trace, makes use of user ID and password information obtained illicitly from one host to compromise another host.
wrong_explanations.D: A negative acknowledgment is a penetration technique that capitalizes on a potential weakness in an operating system that does not handle asynchronous interrupts properly, leaving the system in an unprotected state during such interrupts.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of elliptic curve encryption over RSA encryption?
questions.correct_explanation: The main advantage of elliptical curve cryptography (ECC) over RSA encryption is its computation speed. This is due in part to the use of much smaller keys in the ECC algorithm than in RSA.

wrong_explanations.B: Both encryption methods support digital signatures.
wrong_explanations.C: Both encryption methods are used for public key encryption and distribution.
wrong_explanations.D: Both ECC and RSA offer message integrity controls.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: Which of the following would be the BEST overall control for an Internet business looking for confidentiality,reliability and integrity of data?
questions.correct_explanation: Transport Layer Security (TLS) is used for many ecommerce applications to set up a secure channel for communications that provides confidentiality through a combination of public and symmetric key encryption and integrity through hash message authentication code.

wrong_explanations.B: An intrusion detection system (intrusion detection system (IDS)) will log network activity but is not used for protecting traffic over the Internet.
wrong_explanations.C: Public key infrastructure is used in conjunction with secure sockets layer (SSL) or for securing communications such as ecommerce and email.
wrong_explanations.D: A virtual private network (VPN) is a generic term for a communications tunnel that can provide confidentiality, integrity and authentication (reliability). A VPN can operate at different levels of the Open Systems Interconnection stack and may not always be used in conjunction with encryption. SSL can be called a type of VPN.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following preventive controls BEST helps secure a web application?
questions.correct_explanation: Of the given choices, teaching developers to write secure code is the best way to secure a web application.

wrong_explanations.A: Password masking is a necessary preventive control but is not the best way to secure an application.
wrong_explanations.C: Encryption will protect data but is not sufficient to secure an application because other flaws in coding can compromise the application and data. questions.question: Which of the following antivirus software implementation strategies is the MOST effective in an interconnected enterprise network?
questions.correct_explanation: An important means of controlling the spread of viruses is to deploy an enterprisewide antivirus solution that will monitor and analyze traffic at many points. This provides a layered defense model that is more likely to detect malware regardless of how it comes into the enterprise---through a USB or portable storage, a network, an infected download or malicious web application.

wrong_explanations.A: An effective antivirus solution must be a combination of server-, network-and perimeter-based scanning and protection.
wrong_explanations.C: Only checking for a virus on workstations is not adequate because malware can infect many network devices or servers as well.
wrong_explanations.D: Because malware can enter an enterprise through many different methods, only checking for malware at the perimeter is not enough to protect the enterprise.

questions.question: Which of the following would be of MOST concern to an information systems (IS) auditor reviewing a virtual private network implementation? Computers on the network are located:
questions.correct_explanation: One risk of a virtual private network implementation is the chance of allowing high-risk computers onto the enterprise's network. All machines that are allowed onto the virtual network should be subject to the same security policy. Home computers of third-party (vendor) employees are least subject to the enterprise security policies and, therefore, are high-risk computers. When a computer is hacked and owned, any network that trusts that computer is at risk. Implementation and adherence to enterprise security policy is easier when all computers on the network are on the enterprise's campus.

wrong_explanations.A: On an enterprise's internal network, there should be security policies and controls in place to detect and halt an outside attack that uses an internal machine as a staging platform.
wrong_explanations.B: Computers at the backup site are subject to the enterprise security policy and, therefore, are not high-risk computers.
wrong_explanations.D: Computers on the network that are at the enterprise's remote offices, perhaps with different information systems (IS) and security employees who have different ideas about security, are higher risk than computers in the main office or backup site but have less risk than home computers.

questions.question: The PRIMARY reason for using digital signatures is to ensure data:
questions.correct_explanation: Digital signatures provide integrity because the digital signature of a signed message (file, mail, document, etc.) changes every time a single bit of the document changes; thus, a signed document cannot be altered. A digital signature provides for message integrity, nonrepudiation and proof of origin.

wrong_explanations.A: A digital signature does not address message confidentiality.
wrong_explanations.C: Availability is not related to digital signatures.
wrong_explanations.D: In general, correctness is not related to digital signatures. A digital signature guarantee data integrity, however, it cannot ensure correctness of signed data.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a passive cybersecurity attack?
questions.correct_explanation: Cybersecurity threats/vulnerabilities are divided into passive and active attacks. A passive attack is one that monitors or captures network traffic but does not in any way modify, insert or delete the traffic. Examples of passive attacks include network analysis, eavesdropping and traffic analysis.

wrong_explanations.B: Because masquerading alters the data by modifying the origin, it is an active attack.
wrong_explanations.C: Because a denial-of-service attack floods the network with traffic or sends malformed packets over the network, it is an active attack.
wrong_explanations.D: Because email spoofing alters the email header, it is an active attack.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing security incident management procedures for the enterprise. Which of the following choices is the MOST important consideration?

options.A: Chain of custody of electronic evidence

questions.correct_explanation: The preservation of evidence is the most important consideration in regard to security incident management. If data and evidence are not collected properly, valuable information can be lost and would not be admissible in a court of law should the enterprise decide to pursue litigation.

wrong_explanations.B: System breach notification is an important aspect and, in many cases, may even be required by laws and regulations; however, the security incident may not be a breach and the notification procedure might not apply.
wrong_explanations.C: Escalation procedures to external agencies such as the local police or special agencies dealing in cybercrime are important. However, without proper chain of custody procedures, vital evidence may be lost and would not be admissible in a court of law should the enterprise decide to pursue litigation.
wrong_explanations.D: Although having procedures in place to recover lost data is important, it is critical to ensure that evidence is protected to ensure follow-up and investigation.

questions.question: An accuracy measure for a biometric system is:
questions.correct_explanation: Three main accuracy measures are used for a biometric solution: false-rejection rate (FRR), cross­error rate (CER) and false-acceptance rate (FAR). FRR is a measure of how often valid individuals are rejected. FAR is a measure of how often invalid individuals are accepted. CER is a measure of when the false-rejection rate equals the false-acceptance rate.

wrong_explanations.A: An important consideration in the implementation of biometrics is the time required to process a user. If the system is too slow, then it will impact productivity and lead to frustration. However, this is not an accuracy measure.
wrong_explanations.B: The registration time is a measure of the effort taken to enroll a user in the system. This is not an accuracy measure.
wrong_explanations.C: The file size to retain biometric information varies depending on the type of biometric solution selected. This is not an accuracy measure.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor evaluating logical access controls should FIRST:

options.B: test controls over the access paths to determine if they are functional.
options.C: evaluate the security environment in relation to written policies and practices.

wrong_explanations.C: It is only after the risk is determined and the controls documented that the information systems (IS) auditor can evaluate the security environment to assess its adequacy through review of the written policies, observation of practices and comparison of them to appropriate security good practices.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the goal of business process-driven enterprise architecture? It attempts to better understand an organization in terms of:

questions.question: The review of router access control lists should be conducted during:
questions.correct_explanation: Network security reviews include reviewing router access control lists, port scanning, internal and external connections to the system, etc.

wrong_explanations.A: Environmental reviews examine physical security such as power and physical access. They do not require a review of the router access control lists.
wrong_explanations.C: Business continuity reviews ensure that the business continuity plan is up-to-date, adequate to protect the organization and tested, and do not require a review of the router access control lists.
wrong_explanations.D: Data integrity reviews validate data accuracy and protect from improper alterations, but do not require a review of the router access control lists.

tips: Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: Which of the following components is responsible for the collection of data in an intrusion detection system?
questions.correct_explanation: Sensors are responsible for collecting data. Sensors may be attached to a network, server or other location and may gather data from many points for later analysis.

wrong_explanations.A: Analyzers receive input from sensors and determine the presence of and type of intrusive activity.
wrong_explanations.B: An administration console is the management interface component of an intrusion detection system (IDS).
wrong_explanations.C: A user interface allows the administrators to interact with the IDS.

tips: Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST significant function of an enterprise public key infrastructure and certificate authority employing X.509 digital certificates?

options.A: It provides the public/private key set for the encryption and signature services used by email and file space.
options.B: It binds a digital certificate and its public key to an individual subscriber's identity.
options.C: It provides the authoritative source for employee identity and personal details.
options.D: It provides the authoritative authentication source for object access.

questions.correct_explanation: PKI is primarily used to gain assurance that protected data or services originated from a legitimate source. The process to ensure the validity of the subscriber identity by linking to the digital certificate/public key is strict and rigorous.

wrong_explanations.A: Although some email applications depend on public key infrastructure (PKI)-issued certificates for nonrepudiation, the purpose of PKI is to provide authentication of the individual and link an individual with their private key. The certificate (certification) authority (CA) does not ordinarily create the user's private key.
wrong_explanations.C: Personal details are not stored in or provided by components in the PKI.
wrong_explanations.D: Authentication services within operating systems and applications may be built on PKI-issued certificates, but PKI does not provide authentication services for object access.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: A digital signature contains a message digest to:

options.A: show if the message has been altered after transmission.
options.C: confirm the identity of the originator.
options.D: enable message transmission in a digital format.

questions.correct_explanation: The message digest is calculated and included in a digital signature to prove that the message has not been altered. The message digest sent with the message should have the same value as the recalculation of the digest of the received message.

wrong_explanations.B: The message digest does not define the algorithm; it is there to ensure integrity.
wrong_explanations.C: The message digest does not confirm the identity of the user; it is there to ensure integrity.
wrong_explanations.D: The message digest does not enable the transmission in digital format; it is there to ensure integrity.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: Which of the following manages the digital certificate life cycle to ensure that adequate security and controls exist in digital signature applications related to ecommerce?
questions.correct_explanation: The CA maintains a directory of digital certificates for the reference of those receiving them. It manages the certificate life cycle, including certificate directory maintenance and certificate revocation list (CRL) maintenance and publication.

wrong_explanations.A: A registration authority is an optional entity that is responsible for the administrative tasks associated with registering the end entity that is the subject of the certificate issued by the certificate (certification) authority (CA).
wrong_explanations.C: A CRL is an instrument for checking the continued validity of the certificates for which the CA has responsibility. A certificate that is put on a CRL can no longer be trusted.
wrong_explanations.D: A certification practice statement is a detailed set of rules governing the certificate authority's operations.

tips: Asymmetric crypto: encrypt with the recipient's public key (confidentiality), sign with the sender's private key (authenticity + non-repudiation).

questions.question: A Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP)-based environment is exposed to the Internet. Which of the following BEST ensures that complete encryption and authentication protocols exist for protecting information while transmitted?

options.A: Work is completed in tunnel mode with internet protocol (IP) security.
options.B: A digital signature with RSA has been implemented.
options.C: Digital certificates with RSA are being used.
options.D: Work is being completed in transmission control protocol (TCP) services.

questions.correct_explanation: Tunnel mode with internet protocol (IP) security provides encryption and authentication of the complete IP package. To accomplish this, the authentication header and encapsulating security payload services can be nested. This is known as IP Security.

wrong_explanations.B: A digital signature with RSA provides authentication and integrity but not confidentiality.
wrong_explanations.C: Digital certificates with RSA provide authentication and integrity but do not provide encryption.
wrong_explanations.D: Transmission Control Protocol services do not provide encryption and authentication.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: Digital signatures require the:

options.A: signer to have a public key and the receiver to have a private key.
options.B: signer to have a private key and the receiver to have a public key.
options.C: signer and receiver to have a public key.
options.D: signer and receiver to have a private key.

questions.correct_explanation: Digital signatures are intended to verify to a recipient the integrity of the data and the identity of the sender. The digital signature standard is based on the sender encrypting a digest of the message with their private key and the receiver validating the message with the public key.

wrong_explanations.A: If a sender encrypts a message with a public key, it will provide confidential transmission to the receiver with the private key.
wrong_explanations.C: Asymmetric key cryptography always works with key pairs. Therefore, a message encrypted with a public key can only be opened with a private key.
wrong_explanations.D: Ifboth the sender and receiver have a private key there would be no way to validate the digital signature.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: The feature of a digital signature that ensures that the sender cannot later deny generating and sending the message is called:
questions.correct_explanation: Integrity, authentication, nonrepudiation and replay protection are all features of a digital signature. Nonrepudiation ensures that the claimed sender cannot later deny generating and sending the message.

wrong_explanations.A: Data integrity refers to changes in the plaintext message that would result in the recipient failing to compute the same message hash.
wrong_explanations.B: Because only the claimed sender has the private key used to create the digital signature, authentication ensures that the message has been sent by the claimed sender.
wrong_explanations.D: Replay protection is a method that a recipient can use to check that the message was not intercepted and re-sent (replayed).

tips: Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: During the collection of forensic evidence, which of the following actions would MOST likely result in the destruction or corruption of evidence on a compromised system?

options.A: Dumping the memory content to a file
options.B: Generating disk images of the compromised system
options.D: Removing the system from the network

questions.correct_explanation: Rebooting the system may result in a change in the system state and the loss of files and important evidence stored in memory.

wrong_explanations.A: Copying the memory contents is a normal forensics procedure where possible. Done carefully, it will not corrupt the evidence.
wrong_explanations.B: Proper forensics procedures require creating two copies of the images of the system for analysis. Hash values ensure that the copies are accurate.
wrong_explanations.D: When investigating a system, it is recommended to disconnect it from the network to minimize external infection or access.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing Transport Layer Security enabled websites for the enterprise. Which of the following choices would be the HIGHEST risk?

options.C: Using the same digital certificate for multiple websites

questions.correct_explanation: Self-signed digital certificates are not signed by a certificate (certification) authority (CA) and can be created by anyone. Thus, they can be used by attackers to impersonate a website, which may lead to data theft or perpetrate a man-in-the-middle attack.

wrong_explanations.A: An expired certificate leads to blocked access to the website, leading to unwanted downtime. However, there is no loss of data. Therefore, the comparative risk is lower.
wrong_explanations.C: Using the same digital certificate is not a significant risk. Wildcard digital certificates may be used for multiple subdomain websites.
wrong_explanations.D: 56-bit digital certificates may be needed to connect with older versions of operating system (OS) or browsers. Although they have a lower strength than 128-bit or 256-bit digital certificates, the comparative risk of a self-signed certificate is higher.

tips: Asymmetric crypto: encrypt with the recipient's public key (confidentiality), sign with the sender's private key (authenticity + non-repudiation).

questions.question: Which of the following controls would BEST detect intrusion?

options.A: User IDs and user privileges are granted through authorized procedures.
options.B: Automatic logoff is used when a workstation is inactive for a particular period of time.
options.C: Automatic logoff of the system occurs after a specified number of unsuccessful attempts.
options.D: Unsuccessful logon attempts are monitored by the security administrator.

questions.correct_explanation: Intrusion is detected by the active monitoring and review of unsuccessful logon attempts.

wrong_explanations.A: User IDs and the granting of user privileges define a policy. This is a type of administrative or managerial control that may prevent intrusion but would not detect it.
wrong_explanations.B: Automatic logoff is a method of preventing access through unattended or inactive terminals but is not a detective control.
wrong_explanations.C: Unsuccessful attempts to log on are a method for preventing intrusion, not detecting it.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST control over a guest wireless ID that is given to vendor staff?

options.A: Assignment of a renewable user ID that expires daily.
options.B: A write-once log to monitor the vendor's activities on the system.
options.C: Use of a user ID format similar to that used by employees.
options.D: Ensuring that wireless network encryption is configured properly.

questions.correct_explanation: A renewable user ID that expires daily is a good control because it ensures that wireless access will automatically terminate daily and cannot be used without authorization.

wrong_explanations.B: Although it is recommended to monitor vendor activities while vendor staff are on the system, this is a detective control and, thus, is not as strong as a preventive control.
wrong_explanations.C: The user ID format does not change the overall security of the wireless connection.
wrong_explanations.D: Controls related to the encryption of the wireless network are important; however, access to that network is a more critical issue.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor performing a telecommunication access control review should be concerned PRIMARILY with the:

options.A: maintenance of access logs of usage of various system resources.
options.B: authorization and authentication of the user prior to granting access to system resources.
options.C: adequate protection of stored data on servers by encryption or other means.
options.D: accountability system and the ability to identify any terminal accessing system resources.

questions.correct_explanation: The authorization and authentication of users before granting them access to system resources (networks, servers, applications, etc.) is the most significant aspect in a telecommunication access control review because it is a preventive control. Weak controls at this level can affect all other aspects of security.

wrong_explanations.A: The maintenance of access logs of usage of system resources is a detective control. A preventive control should be used first.
wrong_explanations.C: The adequate protection of data being stored on servers by encryption or other means is a method of protecting stored information and is not a network access issue.
wrong_explanations.D: The accountability system and the ability to identify any tenninal accessing system resources deal with controlling access through the identification of a tenninal or device attempting to connect to the network. This is called node authentication and is not as good as authenticating the user sitting at that node.

tips: Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor suspects an incident is occurring while an audit is being performed on a financial system. What should the IS auditor do FIRST?

options.A: Request that the system be shut down to preserve evidence.
options.C: Ask for immediate suspension of the suspect accounts.
options.D: Investigate the source and nature of the incident.

questions.correct_explanation: Reporting the suspected incident to management will help initiate the incident response process, which is the most appropriate action. Management is responsible for making decisions regarding the appropriate response. It is not the IS auditor's role to respond to incidents during an audit.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor should follow the incident response process of the organization. The auditor is not authorized to shut the system down.
wrong_explanations.C: The IS auditor is not authorized to lead the investigation or to suspend user accounts. The auditor should report the incident to management.
wrong_explanations.D: Management is responsible for setting up and following an incident management plan; that is not the responsibility of the IS auditor.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).

questions.question: When using public key encryption to secure data being transmitted across a network:

options.A: the keys used to encrypt and decrypt the data are public.
options.B: the key used to encrypt the data is private, but the key used to decrypt the data is public.
options.C: the key used to encrypt the data is public, but the key used to decrypt the data is private.
options.D: the keys used to encrypt and decrypt the data are private.

questions.correct_explanation: Public key encryption, also known as asymmetric key cryptography, uses a public key to encrypt the message and a private key to decrypt it.

wrong_explanations.A: The public and private keys always work as a pair-if a public key is used to encrypt a message, the corresponding private key MUST be used to decrypt the message.
wrong_explanations.B: if the message is encrypted with a private key, that will provide proof of origin but not message security or confidentiality.
wrong_explanations.D: Using two private keys is not possible with asymmetric encryption.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: The technique used to ensure security in virtual private networks is called:
questions.correct_explanation: Encapsulation, or tunneling, is a technique used to encrypt the traffic payload so that it can be securely transmitted over an insecure network.

wrong_explanations.B: Wrapping is used where the original packet is wrapped in another packet but is not directly related to security.
wrong_explanations.C: To transform or change the state of communication is not used for security.
wrong_explanations.D: Hashing is used in virtual private networks to ensure message integrity.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: During an audit of a telecommunications system, an information systems (IS) auditor finds that the risk of intercepting data transmitted to and from remote sites is very high. The MOST effective control for reducing this exposure is:
questions.correct_explanation: Encryption of data is the most secure method of protecting confidential data from exposure.

wrong_explanations.B: A callback system is used to ensure that a user is only logging in from a known location. It is not effective to protect the transmitted data from interception.
wrong_explanations.C: Message authentication is used to prove message integrity and source but not confidentiality.
wrong_explanations.D: It is more difficult to intercept traffic traversing a dedicated leased line than it is to intercept data on a shared network, but the only way to really protect the confidentiality of data is to encrypt it.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: An Internet-based attack using password sniffing can:

options.A: enable one party to act as if they are another party.
options.B: cause modification to the contents of certain transactions.
options.C: be used to gain access to systems containing proprietary information.
options.D: result in major problems with billing systems and transaction processing agreements.

questions.correct_explanation: Password sniffing attacks can be used to gain access to systems on which proprietary information is stored.

wrong_explanations.A: Spoofing attacks can be used to enable one party to act as if they are another party.
wrong_explanations.B: Data modification attacks can be used to modify the contents of certain transactions.
wrong_explanations.D: Repudiation of transactions can cause major problems with billing systems and transaction processing agreements.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following controls is the MOST comprehensive in a remote access network with multiple and diverse subsystems?
questions.correct_explanation: The best way to secure remote access is through the use of encrypted VPNs. This allows remote users a secure connection to the main systems.

wrong_explanations.A: A proxy server is a type of firewall installation used as an intermediary to filter and control traffic between internal and external parties.
wrong_explanations.B: Although firewall installations are the primary line of defense, they would need to have encryption and a virtual private network (VPN) to secure remote access traffic.
wrong_explanations.C: A demilitarized zone (DMZ) is an isolated network used to permit outsiders to access certain enterprise information in a semitrusted environment. The DMZ may host a web server or other external facing services. Traffic to a DMZ is not usually encrypted unless it is terminating on a VPN located in the DMZ.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: During an audit of an enterprise that is dedicated to ecommerce, the information systems (IS) manager states that digital signatures are used when receiving communications from customers. To substantiate this, an IS auditor must prove that which of the following is used?

options.A: A biometric, digitalized and encrypted parameter with the customer's public key.
options.B: A hash of the data that is transmitted and encrypted with the customer's private key.
options.C: A hash of the data that is transmitted and encrypted with the customer's public key.
options.D: The customer's scanned signature encrypted with the customer's public key.

questions.correct_explanation: The calculation of a hash, or digest, of the data that are transmitted, and its encryption require the private key of the client (sender) and ls called a signature of the message, or digital signature. The receiver hashes the received message and compares the hash that they compute with the received hash, after the digital signature has been decrypted with the sender's public key. If the hash values are the same, the conclusion is that there is integrity in the data that have arrived, and the origin is authenticated. The concept of encrypting the hash with the private key of the originator provides nonrepudiation because it can only be decrypted with their public key, and the private key would not be known to the recipient. Simply put, in a key-pair situation, anything that can be decrypted by a sender's public key must have been encrypted with their private key, so they must have been the sender (i.e., nonrepudiation).

wrong_explanations.A: Biometrics are not used in digital signatures or public key encryption.
wrong_explanations.C: It is not correct to encrypt the hash with the customer's public key because the recipient would need access to the customer's private key to decrypt the digital signature.
wrong_explanations.D: A scan of the customer's signature is known as a digitized signature, not a digital signature, and is of little or no value in this scenario.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: When planning an audit of a network setup, an information systems (IS) auditor should give highest priority to obtaining which of the following network documentation?
questions.correct_explanation: The wiring and schematic diagram of the network is necessary to carry out a network audit. The information systems (IS) auditor needs to know what equipment, configuration and addressing is used on the network to perform an audit of the network setup.

wrong_explanations.B: When performing an audit of network setup, the users' lists would not be of value.
wrong_explanations.C: Application lists are not required to audit network configuration.
wrong_explanations.D: Backup and recovery procedures are important but not as important as knowing the network layout.

tips: Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following should an information systems (IS) auditor be MOST concerned about in a financial application?

options.A: Programmers have access to source code in the user acceptance testing environment.
options.B: Secondary controls are documented for identified role conflicts.
options.C: The information security officer does not authorize all application changes.
options.D: Programmers have access to the production database.

questions.correct_explanation: Programmers having access to the production database is considered a separation of duties conflict.

wrong_explanations.A: Programmers who have access to application source code are not of concern to the information systems (IS) auditor because programmers need access to source code to do their jobs. The user acceptance testing (UAT) environment is separate from the production environment, and changes cannot be moved into the production environment without prior authorization.
wrong_explanations.B: When separation of duties conflicts are identified, secondary controls should be in place to mitigate risk. Although the IS auditor reviews secondary controls, in this case, the greater concern is programmers having access to the production database.
wrong_explanations.C: The information security officer is not likely to authorize all application changes; therefore, this is not a concern for an IS auditor.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MAIN reason an enterprise should have an incident response plan? The plan helps to:

options.A: ensure prompt communication of adverse events to relevant management.
options.B: contain costs related to maintaining disaster recovery plan capabilities.
options.C: ensure that customers are promptly notified of issues, such as security breaches.
options.D: minimize the duration and impact of system outages and security incidents.

questions.correct_explanation: An incident response plan helps minimize the impact of an incident because it provides a controlled response to incidents. The phases of the plan include planning, detection, evaluation, containment, eradication, escalation, response, recovery, reporting, post-incident review and a review of lessons learned.

wrong_explanations.A: Incident response plans generally deal with a wide range of possible issues. Although it is important to have proper communication of an adverse event within the enterprise, the primary objective is to reduce impact of incidents.
wrong_explanations.B: An effective incident response plan can minimize damage to the enterprise, which minimizes costs, but the main purpose of the incident response plan is to minimize damage. Possible damage can include nonfinancial metrics, such as damage to the enterprise's reputation.
wrong_explanations.C: Although an incident response plan includes elements such as when and how to contact customers about a significant incident, the primary purpose of the plan is to minimize the impact.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Email message authenticity and confidentiality is BEST achieved by signing the message using the:

options.A: sender's private key and encrypting the message using the receiver's public key.
options.B: sender's public key and encrypting the message using the receiver's private key.
options.C: receiver's private key and encrypting the message using the sender's public key.
options.D: receiver's public key and encrypting the message using the sender's private key.

questions.correct_explanation: By signing the message with the sender's private key, the receiver can verify its authenticity using the sender's public key. Encrypting with the receiver's public key provides confidentiality.

wrong_explanations.B: Signing can only occur using the sender's private key.
wrong_explanations.C: The sender does not have access to the receiver's private key.
wrong_explanations.D: By encrypting the message with the receiver's public key, only the receiver can decrypt the message using their own private key. The receiver's private key is confidential and, therefore, unknown to the sender. Messages encrypted using the sender's private key can be read by anyone with the sender's public key.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: An organization is considering connecting a critical PC-based system to the Internet. Which of the following provides the BEST protection against hacking?
questions.correct_explanation: An application-level gateway is the best way to protect against hacking because it can be configured with detailed rules that describe the type of user or connection that is or is not permitted. It analyzes, in detail, each package-not only in layers one through four of the Open System Interconnection model, but also layers five through seven, which means that it reviews the commands of each higher-level protocol (Hypertext Transmission Protocol, File Transfer Protocol, Simple Network Management Protocol, etc.).

wrong_explanations.B: For a remote access server, there is a device (server) that asks for a username and password before entering the network. This is good when accessing private networks, but it can be mapped or scanned from the Internet, creating security exposure.
wrong_explanations.C: Proxy servers can provide excellent protection, but depending on the type of proxy, they may not be able to examine traffic as effectively as an application gateway. Proxy servers require experienced personnel to manage them. Applications can use different ports for the different sections of the program.
wrong_explanations.D: Port scanning is used to detect vulnerabilities or open ports on a network, but not when trying to control what comes from the Internet or when all the ports available need to be controlled. For example, the port for Ping (echo request) can be blocked and the internet protocol (IP) addresses would be available for the application and browsing but would not respond to Ping.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST secure and economical method for connecting a private network over the Internet in a small-to medium-sized enterprise?
questions.correct_explanation: The most secure method is a virtual private network (VPN), using encryption, authentication and tunneling to allow data to travel securely from a private network to the Internet.

wrong_explanations.B: A dedicated line is quite expensive and only needed when there are specific confidentiality and availability needs.
wrong_explanations.C: A leased line is an expensive but private option, but rarely a good option today.
wrong_explanations.D: Integrated services digital network is not encrypted and needs additional security to be a valid option.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: The potential for unauthorized system access by way of terminals or workstations within an enterprise's facility is increased when:

options.A: connecting points are available in the facility to connect laptops to the network.
options.B: users take precautions to keep their passwords confidential.
options.C: terminals with password protection are located in insecure locations.
options.D: terminals are located within the facility in small clusters under the supervision of an administrator.

questions.correct_explanation: Any person with wrongful intentions can connect a laptop to the network. The insecure connecting points make unauthorized access possible if the individual has knowledge of a valid user ID and password. The other choices are controls for preventing unauthorized network access.

wrong_explanations.B: If system passwords are not readily available for intruders to use, they must guess, introducing an additional factor and requires time.
wrong_explanations.C: System passwords provide protection against unauthorized use of terminals located in insecure locations.
wrong_explanations.D: Supervision is a very effective control when used to monitor access to a small operating unit or production resources.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following functions is performed by a virtual private network (VPN)?

options.A: Hiding information from sniffers on the net

questions.correct_explanation: A virtual private network (VPN) hides information from sniffers on the Internet using tunneling. It works based on encapsulation and encryption of sensitive traffic.

wrong_explanations.B: A VPN does support security policies related to secure communications, but its primary purpose is to protect data in transit.
wrong_explanations.C: A VPN does not check the content of packets, so it cannot detect misuse or mistakes.
wrong_explanations.D: A VPN is not used to regulate access. A user may have to log in to use a VPN, but that is not the purpose of the VPN.

tips: Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Applying a digital signature to data traveling in a network provides:
questions.correct_explanation: A digital signature is created by signing a hash of a message with the private key of the sender. This provides for the integrity (through the hash) and the proof of origin (nonrepudiation) of the message.

wrong_explanations.A: A digital signature does not encrypt the message, so it cannot provide confidentiality.
wrong_explanations.B: A digital signature does not encrypt the message, so it cannot provide security.
wrong_explanations.D: A digital signature does not provide confidentiality.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: Which of the following would an information systems (IS) auditor consider a weakness when performing an audit of an enterprise that uses a public key infrastructure with digital certificates for its business-to-consumer transactions via the Internet?

options.A: Customers are widely dispersed geographically, but the certificate (certification) authority (CA) are not.
options.B: Customers can make their transactions from any computer or mobile device.
options.C: The CA has several data processing subcenters to administer certificates.
options.D: The enterprise is the owner of the CA.

questions.correct_explanation: if the CA belongs to the same enterprise, this poses a risk. The management of a CA must be based on trusted and secure procedures. If the enterprise has not set in place the controls to manage the registration, distribution and revocation of certificates, this can lead to a compromise of the certificates and loss of trust.

wrong_explanations.A: It is common to use a single certificate (certification) authority (CA). They do not need to be geographically dispersed.
wrong_explanations.B: The use of public key infrastructure and certificates allows flexible secure communications from many devices.
wrong_explanations.C: The CA will often have redundancy and failover capabilities to alternate data centers.

tips: Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST reliable method to ensure identity of the sender for messages transferred across the Internet?

questions.question: The MOST serious challenge in the operation of an intrusion detection system is:

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor performing an audit has determined that developers have been granted administrative access to the virtual machine management console to manage their own servers used for software development and testing. options.B: Developers can gain elevated access to production servers.

wrong_explanations.B: When properly configured, the administrative console of a virtual server host does not allow an individual to bypass the authentication of the guest operating system (OS) to access the server. wrong_explanations.C: Although there can be instances where a software development team might use resource-intensive applications that can cause performance issues for the virtual host, the greater risk is the ability to de-provision VMs.

There may be occasions when the application ID needs to be used by change control in the production environment.
wrong_explanations.D: Although the lack of a strong password policy and configuration can result in compromised accounts, the risk is lower than if the application ID password is compromised because the application ID password does not allow for traceability.

questions.question: An enterprise determined that its website was compromised, and a rootkit was installed on the server hosting the application. Which of the following choices would have MOST likely prevented the incident?
questions.correct_explanation: A host-based intrusion prevention system (IPS) prevents unauthorized changes to the host. If a malware attack attempted to install a rootkit, the IPS would refuse to permit the installation without the consent of an administrator.

wrong_explanations.B: A network-based intrusion detection system (IDS) relies on attack signatures based on known exploits and attack patterns. If the IDS is not kept up-to-date with the latest signatures, or the attacker is able to create or gain access to an exploit unknown to the IDS, it will go undetected. A web server exploit performed through the web application itself, such as a Structured Query Language injection attack, would not appear to be an attack to the network-based IDS.
wrong_explanations.C: A firewall, by itself, does not protect a web server because the ports required for users to access the web server must be open in the firewall. Web server attacks are typically performed over the same ports that are open for normal web traffic. Therefore, a firewall does not protect the web server.
wrong_explanations.D: Operating system (OS) patching makes exploitation of the server more difficult for the attacker and less likely. However, attacks on the web application and server OS may succeed based on issues unrelated to any unpatched server vulnerabilities, and the host-based IPS should detect any attempts to change files on the server, regardless of how access was obtained.

Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: The role of the certificate (certification) authority (CA) as a third party is to:

options.A: provide secure communication and networking services based on certificates.
options.B: host a repository of certificates with the corresponding public and secret keys issued by that CA.
options.C: act as a trusted intermediary between two communication partners.
options.D: confirm the identity of the entity owning a certificate issued by that CA.

questions.correct_explanation: The primary activity of a CA is to issue certificates. The primary role of the CA is to check the identity of the entity owning a certificate and to confirm the integrity of any certificate it issued.

wrong_explanations.A: Providing a communication infrastructure is not a certificate (certification) authority (CA) activity.
wrong_explanations.B: The secret keys belonging to the certificates are not archived at the CA.
wrong_explanations.C: The CA can contribute to authenticating the communicating partners to each other, but the CA is not involved in the communication stream itself.

tips: Asymmetric crypto: encrypt with the recipient's public key (confidentiality), sign with the sender's private key (authenticity + non-repudiation).

questions.question: Which of the fo11owing types of penetration tests effectively evaluates the incident handling and response capability of the system administrator?
questions.correct_explanation: In double-blind testing, the penetration tester has little or limited knowledge about the target system, and personnel at the target site are not informed that a test is being performed. Because the administrator and security staff at the target are not aware of the test, it can effectively evaluate the incident handling and response capability of the system administrator.

wrong_explanations.A: In targeted testing, penetration testers are provided with information related to target and network design and the target's IT team is aware of the testing activities.
wrong_explanations.B: Internal testing refers to attacks and control circumvention attempts on the target from within the perimeter. The system administrator is typically aware of the testing activities.
wrong_explanations.D: External testing is a generic term that refers to attacks and control circumvention attempts on the target from outside the target system. The system administrator may or may not be aware of the testing activities, so this is not the correct answer. (Note: Rather than concentrating on specific terms, certified information systems auditor (CISA) candidates should understand the differences between various types of penetration testing.)

questions.question: Email traffic from the lnternet is routed via firewall-1 to the mail gateway. Mail is routed from the mail gateway, via firewall-2, to the mail recipients in the internal network. This may have been caused by an attack from a hacker. After the IDS has logged the suspicious traffic, it may signal firewall-2 to close, thus preventing damage to the internal network. After closing firewall-2, the malfunctioning of firewall-1 can be investigated. The IDS should trigger the closing of firewall-2 either automatically or by manual intervention. Between the detection by the IDS and a response from the system administrator, valuable time can be lost, in which a hacker can also compromise firewall-2.

questions.question: An organization has experienced a large amount of traffic being re-routed from its Voice-over Internet Protocol packet network. The organization believes it is a victim of eavesdropping. Which of the following can result in eavesdropping of Voice-over Internet Protocol (VoIP) traffic?

options.A: Corruption of the Address Resolution Protocol cache in Ethernet switches
options.B: Use of a default administrator password on the analog phone switch
options.C: Deploying virtual local area networks VLANs without enabling encryption
options.D: End users having access to software tools such as packet sniffer applications

questions.correct_explanation: On an Ethernet switch, there is a data table known as the address resolution protocol (ARP) cache that stores mappings between media access control and internet protocol (IP) addresses. During normal operations, Ethernet switches only allow directed traffic to flow between the ports involved in the conversation and no other ports can see that traffic. However, if the ARP cache is intentionally corrupted with an ARP poisoning attack, some Ethernet switches simply flood the directed traffic to all ports of the switch, which can allow an attacker to monitor traffic not normally visible to the port where the attacker was connected, and thereby eavesdrop on Voice-over Internet Protocol (VoIP) traffic.

wrong_explanations.B: VoIP systems do not use analog switches and inadequate administrator security controls are not an issue.
wrong_explanations.C: VoIP data are not normally encrypted in a local area network (LAN) environment because the controls regarding virtual local area network (VLAN) security are adequate.
wrong_explanations.D: Most software tools, such as packet sniffers, cannot make changes to LAN devices, such as the VLAN configuration of an Ethernet switch used for VoIP. Therefore, the use of software utilities of this type is not a risk.

tips: Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

wrong_explanations.B: A network-based IDS placed between the Internet and the firewall will detect attack attempts, whether they are or are not noticed by the firewall.
wrong_explanations.C: Placing an IDS outside of the web server will identify attacks directed at the web server but will not detect attacks missed by the firewall.
wrong_explanations.D: Placing the IDS after the web server would identify attacks that have made it past the web server but will not indicate whether the firewall would have been able to detect the attacks.

questions.question: Which of the following choices BEST helps information owners to properly classify data?

options.C: Use of an automated data leak prevention tool
options.D: Understanding which people need to access the data
