questions.question: An enterprise provides information to its supply chain partners and customers through an extranet infrastructure. Which of the following should be the GREATEST concern to an information systems (lS) auditor reviewing the firewall security architecture?

options.A: A secure sockets layer (SSL) has been implemented for user authentication and remote administration of the firewall.
options.B: Firewall policies are updated based on changing requirements.
options.C: Inbound traffic is blocked unless the traffic type and connections have been specifically permitted.
options.D: The firewall is placed on top of the commercial operating system (OS) with all default installation options.

questions.correct_explanation: The greatest concern when implementing firewalls on top of commercial operating systems (OSs) is the potential presence of vulnerabilities that can undermine the security posture of the firewall platform itself. In most circumstances, when commercial firewalls are breached, that breach is facilitated by vulnerabilities in the underlying OS. Keeping all installation options available on the system further increases the risk of vulnerabilities and exploits.

wrong_explanations.A: Using secure sockets layer (SSL) for firewall administration is important because changes in user and supply chain partners' roles and profiles will be dynamic.
wrong_explanations.B: lt is appropriate to maintain the firewall policies as needed.
wrong_explanations.C: It is prudent to block all inbound traffic to an extranet unless permitted.

tips: GREATEST risk/concern questions reward the option with the broadest blast radius, irreversibility, or regulatory exposure.
Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: An enterprise is proposing to establish a wireless local area network (WLAN). Management asks the information systems (IS) auditor to recommend security controls for the WLAN. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate recommendation?

options.A: Physically secure wireless access points to prevent tampering.
options.B: Use service set identifiers that clearly identify the enterprise.
options.C: Encrypt traffic using the wired equivalent privacy (WEP) mechanism.
options.D: Implement the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) to allow active monitoring.

questions.correct_explanation: Physically securing access points, such as wireless routers, and preventing theft address the risk of malicious parties tampering with device settings. If access points can be physically reached, it is often a simple matter to restore weak default passwords and encryption keys, or to totally remove authentication and encryption from the network.

wrong_explanations.B: Service set identifiers should not be used to identify the enterprise, because hackers can associate the wireless local area network (WLAN) with a known enterprise, and this increases their motivation to attack and, potentially, the information available to do so.
wrong_explanations.C: The original wired equivalent privacy (WEP) security mechanism has been demonstrated to have a number of exploitable weaknesses. The more recently developed Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA) and WPA 2 standards represent considerably more secure means of authentication and encryption.
wrong_explanations.D: Installing Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) on wireless access points can open up security vulnerabilities. If SNMP is required at all, then SNMP v3, which has stronger authentication mechanisms than earlier versions, should be deployed.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.
Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: Which of the following situations would increase the likelihood of fraud?

options.A: Application programmers are implementing changes to data in the production database.
options.B: Administrators are implementing vendor patches to vendor-supplied software without following change control procedures.
options.C: Operations support staff members are implementing changes to batch schedules.
options.D: Database administrators (DBA) are implementing changes to data structures.

questions.correct_explanation: Production programs are used for processing enterprise data. It is imperative that controls on changes to production programs are stringent. Lack of control in this area can result in application programs being modified to manipulate the data.

wrong_explanations.B: The lack of change control is a serious risk-but if the changes are only vendor-supplied patches to vendor software then the risk is minimal.
wrong_explanations.C: The implementation of changes to batch schedules by operations support staff affects the scheduling of the batches only; it does not impact the live data unless jobs are run in the wrong sequence.
wrong_explanations.D: Database administrators (DBA) are required to implement changes to data structures. This is required for reorganization of the database to allow for additions, modifications or deletions of fields or tables in the database.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: A consulting firm created a file transfer protocol (FTP) site for the purpose of receiving financial data and communicated the site's address, user ID and password to the financial services enterprise in separate email messages. The enterprise is to transmit its data to the FTP site after manually encrypting the data. The information systems (IS) auditor's GREATEST concern with this process is that:

options.A: The users may not remember to manually encrypt the data before transmission.
options.B: The site credentials were sent to the financial services enterprise via email.
options.C: Personnel at the consulting firm may obtain access to sensitive data.
options.D: The use of a shared user ID to the FTP site does not allow for user accountability.

questions.correct_explanation: if the data is not encrypted, an unauthorized external party may download sensitive enterprise data.

wrong_explanations.B: Although the possibility exists that the logon information was captured from the emails, data should be encrypted, so the theft of the data would not allow the attacker to read them.
wrong_explanations.C: Some of the employees at the consulting firm will have access to the sensitive data and the consulting firm must have procedures in place to protect the data.
wrong_explanations.D: Tracing accountability is of minimal concern compared to the compromise of sensitive data.

tips: GREATEST risk/concern questions reward the option with the broadest blast radius, irreversibility, or regulatory exposure.

questions.question: Java applets and Active X controls are distributed programs that execute in the background of a client web browser. This practice is considered reasonable when:

options.B: a secure web connection is used.
options.C: the source of the executable file is certain.
options.D: the host website is part of the enterprise.

questions.correct_explanation: Acceptance of these mechanisms should be based on established trust. The control is provided by only knowing the source and then allowing the acceptance of the applets. Hostile applets can be received from anywhere.

wrong_explanations.A: There should always be a firewall on an Internet connection; however, whether to allow active models is a decision made depending on the source of the module.
wrong_explanations.B: A secure web connection provides confidentiality. Neither a secure web connection nor a firewall can identify an executable file as friendly.
wrong_explanations.D: Hosting the website as part of the enterprise is impractical. The client will accept the program if the parameters are established to do so.

tips: Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following controls will MOST effectively detect the presence of bursts of errors in network transmissions?
questions.correct_explanation: The cyclic redundancy check (CRC) can check for a block of transmitted data. The workstations generate the CRC and transmit it with the data. The receiving workstation computes a CRC and compares it to the transmitted CRC. If both of them are equal, then the block is assumed error free. In this case (such as, in parity error or echo check), multiple errors can be detected. In general, CRC can detect all single-bit and double-bit errors.

wrong_explanations.A: Parity check (known as vertical redundancy check) also involves adding a bit (known as the parity bit) to each character during transmission. In this case, where there is a presence of bursts of errors (i.e., impulsing noise during high transmission rates), it has a reliability of approximately 50 percent. At higher transmission rates, this limitation is significant.
wrong_explanations.B: Echo checks detect line errors by retransmitting data to the sending device for comparison with the original transmission.
wrong_explanations.C: A block sum check is a form of parity checking and has a low level of reliability.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.
Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following types of transmission media provide the BEST security against unauthorized access?
questions.correct_explanation: Fiber-optic cables have proven to be more secure and more difficult to tap than the other media.

wrong_explanations.A: Twisted pair, coaxial and copper wire traffic can be monitored with inexpensive equipment.
wrong_explanations.B: Twisted pair cabling is a form of copper wire, and although shielding affords some degree of protection from interference, it does not improve security against unauthorized access.
wrong_explanations.D: Coaxial cable can be monitored with relative ease.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST audit procedure to determine if a firewall is configured in compliance with the enterprise security policy?

options.D: Review the device's log file for recent attacks.

questions.correct_explanation: A review of the parameter settings provides a good basis for comparison of the actual configuration to the security policy and provides audit evidence documentation.

wrong_explanations.B: An interview with the firewall administrator will not ensure that the firewall is configured correctly.
wrong_explanations.C: Reviewing the actual procedures is good but will not ensure that the firewall rules are correct and compliant with policy.
wrong_explanations.D: Recent attacks may indicate problems with the firewall but will not ensure that it is correctly configured.

Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing the network infrastructure of a call center and determines that the internal telephone system is based on Voice-over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technology. Which of the following is the GREATEST concern?

options.A: Voice communication uses the same equipment that is used for data communication.
options.B: Ethernet switches are not protected by uninterrupted power supply units.
options.C: Voice communication is not encrypted on the local network.
options.D: The team that supports the data network also is responsible for the telephone system.

questions.correct_explanation: VoIP telephone systems use the LAN infrastructure of an enterprise for communication, typically using Ethernet connectivity to connect individual phones to the system. Most enterprises have a backup power supply for the main servers and systems, but typically do not have uninterrupted power supply units for the LAN switches. In the case of even a brief power outage, not having backup power on all network devices makes it impossible to send or receive phone calls, which is a concern, particularly in a call center.

wrong_explanations.A: Voice-over Internet Protocol (VoIP) telephone systems use the local area network (LAN) infrastructure of an enterprise for communication, which can save on wiring cost and simplify the installation and support of the telephone system. This use of shared infrastructure is a benefit of VoIP and therefore is not a concern.
wrong_explanations.C: VoIP devices do not normally encrypt the voice traffic on the local network, so this is not a concern. Typically, a VoIP phone system connects to a telephone enterprise voice circuit, which is not normally encrypted. If the system uses the Internet for connectivity, then encryption is required.
wrong_explanations.D: VoIP telephone systems use the LAN infrastructure of an enterprise for comm uni cation, so the personnel who support and maintain that infrastructure are now responsible for the data and voice network by default. Therefore, this is not a concern.

tips: GREATEST risk/concern questions reward the option with the broadest blast radius, irreversibility, or regulatory exposure.
Confidentiality requires encryption at rest AND in transit — picking only one usually leaves an exploitable gap.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST ensures continuity of a wide area network (WAN) across the enterprise?

options.C: A repair contract with a service provider
options.D: A duplicate machine alongside each server

questions.correct_explanation: Alternative routing ensures that the network will continue if a communication device fails or if a link is severed because message rerouting can be automatic.

wrong_explanations.B: System backup will not afford protection for a networking failure.
wrong_explanations.C: The repair contract will almost always result in some lost time and is not as effective as permanent alternative routing.
wrong_explanations.D: Standby servers will not provide continuity if a link is severed.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: An enterprise is planning to deploy an outsourced cloud-based application that is used to track job applicant data for the human resources department. Which of the following should be the GREATEST concern to an information systems (IS) auditor?

options.A: The service level agreement (SLA) ensures strict limits for uptime and performance.
options.B: The cloud provider will not agree to an unlimited right-to-audit as part of the SLA.
options.C: The SLA is not explicit regarding the disaster recovery plan capabilities of the cloud provider.
options.D: The cloud provider's physical data centers are in multiple cities and countries.

questions.correct_explanation: Having data in multiple countries is the greatest concern because HR applicant data can contain personally identifiable information. There may be legal compliance issues if these data are stored in a country with different laws regarding data privacy. Although the enterprise is bound by the privacy laws where it is based, it may not have legal recourse if a data breach happens in a jurisdiction where the same laws do not apply.

wrong_explanations.A: Although this application may have strict requirements for availability, it is assumed that the service level agreement (SLA) would contain these same elements; therefore, this is not a concern.
wrong_explanations.B: The right-to-audit clause is good to have, but there are limits on how a cloud service provider may interpret this requirement. The task of reviewing and assessing all the controls in place at a multinational cloud provider would likely be a costly and time-consuming exercise; therefore, such a requirement may be of limited value.
wrong_explanations.C: Because the SLA normally specifies uptime requirements, the means used to achieve those goals (which include the specific disaster recovery plan capabilities of the provider) are typically not reviewed in-depth by the customer, nor are they typically specified in an SLA.

tips: GREATEST risk/concern questions reward the option with the broadest blast radius, irreversibility, or regulatory exposure.

questions.question: An enterprise is reviewing its contract with a cloud computing provider. For which of the following reasons would the enterprise want to remove a lock-in clause from the cloud service contract?
questions.correct_explanation: It may be important for the client to secure portability of their system assets (i.e., the right to transfer from one vendor to another).

wrong_explanations.A: Removing the customer lock-in clause will not secure availability of the systems resources stored in a cloud computing environment. When drawing up a contract with a cloud service provider, the ideal practice is to remove the customer lock-in clause.
wrong_explanations.C: Agility refers to efficiency of solutions enabling enterprises to respond to business needs faster. This is a desirable quality of cloud computing.
wrong_explanations.D: Scalability is the strength of cloud computing through the ability to adjust service levels according to changing business circumstances. Therefore, this is not the best option.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing the enterprise's IT environment and identified that the IT operations team implemented an enhanced level of security over data. Which of the following object-oriented technology characteristic is MOST likely be implemented by the IT operations team?
questions.correct_explanation: Encapsulation is a property of objects, and it prevents accessing either properties or methods that have not been previously defined as public. This means that any implementation of the behavior of an object is not accessible. An object defines a communication interface with the exterior and only that which belongs to that interface can be accessed.

wrong_explanations.A: In object-oriented systems, an object is called by another module and inherits its data from the calling module. This does not affect security.
wrong_explanations.B: Dynamic warehousing is not related to the security of object-oriented technology.
wrong_explanations.D: Polymorphism is the principle of creating different objects that will behave differently depending on the input. This is not a security feature.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: A review of wide area network (WAN) usage discovers that traffic on one communication line between sites, synchronously linking the master and standby database, peaks at 96 percent of the line capacity. An information systems (IS) auditor should conclude that:

options.A: analysis is required to determine if a pattern emerges that results in a service loss for a short period of time.
options.B: WAN capacity is adequate for the maximum traffic demands because saturation has not been reached.
options.C: the line should immediately be replaced by one with a larger capacity to provide approximately 85 percent saturation.
options.D: users should be instructed to reduce their traffic demands or distribute them across all service hours to flatten bandwidth consumption.

questions.correct_explanation: The peak at 96 percent can be the result of a one-off incident (e.g., a user downloading a large amount of data); therefore, analysis to establish whether this is a regular pattern and what causes this behavior should be carried out before expenditure on a larger line capacity is recommended.

wrong_explanations.B: A peak traffic load of 96 percent is approaching a critical level, and the auditor should not assume that capacity is adequate at this time or for the foreseeable future. Further investigation is required.
wrong_explanations.C: If the peak is established to be a regular occurrence without any other opportunities for mitigation (usage of bandwidth reservation protocol or other types of prioritizing network traffic), the line should be replaced because there is the risk of loss of service as the traffic approaches 100 percent. At this point, further research is required.
wrong_explanations.D: If the peak traffic load is a rare one-off occurrence or if traffic can be reengineered to transfer at other time frames, then user education may be an option. Further investigation will be required.

tips: Security controls layer: prevent → detect → respond → recover. Don't pick a single control where the question implies multiple layers are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST limits the impact of server failures in a distributed environment?
questions.correct_explanation: Clustering allows two or more servers to work as a unit so that when one of them fails, the other takes over.

wrong_explanations.A: Redundant pathways will minimize the impact of channel communications failures but will not address the problem of server failure.
wrong_explanations.C: Dial backup lines will minimize the impact of channel communications failures but not a server failure.
wrong_explanations.D: Standby power provides an alternative power source in the event of an energy failure but does not address the problem of a server failure.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
In any physical/safety scenario, life safety is always the first priority — system, asset and data concerns come after.

questions.question: The MAIN reason for requiring that all computer clocks across an enterprise are synchronized is to:

options.A: prevent omission or duplication of transactions.
options.B: ensure smooth data transition from client machines to servers.
options.C: ensure that email messages have accurate time stamps.

questions.correct_explanation: During an investigation of incidents, audit logs are used as evidence, and the time stamp information in them is useful. If the clocks are not synchronized, investigations will be more difficult, because a timeline of events occurring on different systems might not be easily established.

wrong_explanations.A: The possibility of omission or duplication of transactions will not happen due to lack of clock synchronization.
wrong_explanations.B: Data transfer has nothing to do with the time stamp.
wrong_explanations.C: Although the time stamp on an email may not be accurate, this is not a significant issue.

questions.question: When reviewing the configuration of network devices, an information systems (IS) auditor should FIRST identify:

options.A: the good practices for the type of network devices deployed.
options.B: whether components of the network are missing.
options.C: the importance of the network devices in the topology.
options.D: whether subcomponents of the network are being used appropriately.

questions.correct_explanation: The first step is to understand the importance and role of the network device within the enterprise 's network topology.

wrong_explanations.A: After understanding the devices in the network, a good practice for using the device should be reviewed to ensure that there are no anomalies within the configuration.
wrong_explanations.B: Identification of which component is missing can only be known after reviewing and understanding the topology and a good practice for deployment of the device in the network.
wrong_explanations.D: Identification of which subcomponent is being used inappropriately can only be known after reviewing and understanding the topology and a good practice for deployment of the device in the network.

questions.question: Which of the following will BEST maintain the integrity of a firewall log?

options.A: Granting access to log information only to administrators
options.B: Capturing log events in the operating system (OS) layer
options.C: Writing dual logs onto separate storage media
options.D: Sending log information to a dedicated third-party log server

questions.correct_explanation: Establishing a dedicated third-party log server and logging events in it is the best procedure for maintaining the integrity of a firewall log. When access control to the log server is adequately maintained, the risk of unauthorized log modification is mitigated, therefore improving the integrity of log information.

wrong_explanations.A: To enforce segregation/separation of duties (SoD), administrators should not have access to log files. This primarily contributes to the assurance of confidentiality rather than integrity.
wrong_explanations.B: There are many ways to capture log information-through the application layer, network layer, operating systems (OSs) layer, etc. However, there is no log integrity advantage in capturing events in the OS layer.
wrong_explanations.C: If it is a highly mission-critical information system, it may be nice to run the system with a dual log mode. Having logs in two different storage devices will primarily contribute to the assurance of the availability of log information, rather than maintaining its integrity.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
Access decisions default to least privilege and need-to-know — the data owner authorizes; the custodian implements; the auditor verifies.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor reviewing a cloud computing environment that is managed by a third party should be MOST concerned when:

options.A: The enterprise is not permitted to assess the controls in the participating vendor's site.
options.B: The service level agreement (SLA) does not address the responsibility of the vendor in the case of a security breach.
options.C: Laws and regulations are different in the countries of the enterprise and the vendor.
options.D: The enterprise is using an older version of a browser and is vulnerable to certain types of security risk.

questions.correct_explanation: Administration of cloud computing occurs over the Internet and involves more than one participating entity. It is the responsibility of each of the partners in the cloud computing environment to take care of security issues in their own environments. When there is a security breach, the party responsible for the breach should be identified and made accountable. This is not possible if the service level agreement (SLA) does not address the responsibilities of the partners during a security breach.

wrong_explanations.A: The information systems (IS) auditor has no role to play if the contract between the parties does not provide for assessment of controls in the other vendor's site.
wrong_explanations.C: The IS auditor should ensure that the contract addresses the differing laws and regulations in the countries of the enterprise and the vendor, but having different laws and regulations is not a problem.
wrong_explanations.D: The IS auditor can make suggestions to the audited entity to use appropriate patches or switch over to safer browsers, and then the IS auditor can follow up on the action taken.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: Which one of the following can be used to provide automated assurance that proper data files are being used during processing?
questions.correct_explanation: A file header record provides assurance that proper data files are being used, and it allows for automatic checking.

wrong_explanations.B: Although version usage provides assurance that the correct file and version are being used, it does not allow for automatic checking.
wrong_explanations.C: Parity checking is a data integrity validation method typically used by a data transfer program. Although parity checking may help to ensure that data and program files are transferred successfully, it does not help to ensure that the proper data or program files are being used.
wrong_explanations.D: File security controls cannot be used to provide assurance that proper data files are being used and cannot allow for automatic checking.

questions.question: A cyclic redundancy check is commonly used to determine the:
questions.correct_explanation: The accuracy of blocks of data transfers, such as data transfer from hard disks, is validated by a cyclic redundancy check.

wrong_explanations.A: Accuracy of data input can be enforced by data validation controls, such as picklists, cross checks, reasonableness checks, control totals and allowed character checks.
wrong_explanations.B: A checksum or digital signature is commonly used to validate the integrity of a downloaded program or other transferred data.
wrong_explanations.C: Encryption adequacy is driven by the sensitivity of the data to be protected and algorithms that determine how long it will take to break a specific encryption method.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is performing a review of a network. Users report that the network is slow and web pages periodically time out. The IS auditor confirms the users' feedback and reports the findings to the network manager. The most appropriate action for the network management team should be to FIRST:

options.A: use a protocol analyzer to perform network analysis and review error logs of local area network (LAN) equipment.
options.B: take steps to increase the bandwidth of the connection to the Internet.
options.C: create a baseline using a protocol analyzer and implement quality of service to ensure that critical business applications work as intended.
options.D: implement virtual local area networks (VLANs) to segment the network and ensure performance.

questions.correct_explanation: In this case, the first step is to identify the problem through review and analysis of network traffic. Using a protocol analyzer and reviewing the log files of the related switches or routers determine whether there is a configuration issue or hardware malfunction.

wrong_explanations.B: Although increasing Internet bandwidth may be required, this may not be needed if the performance issue is due to a different problem or error condition.
wrong_explanations.C: Although creating a baseline and implementing quality of service ensures that critical applications have the appropriate bandwidth, in this case, the performance issue may be related to misconfiguration or equipment malfunction.
wrong_explanations.D: Although implementing virtual local area networks (VLANs) may be a good practice for ensuring adequate performance, in this case, the issue may be related to misconfigurations or equipment malfunction.

tips: When a question asks for the FIRST step, look for the foundational action that enables every later step (planning before execution, risk assessment before scope, identification before evaluation).

questions.question: In a small enterprise, an employee performs computer operations and, when the situation demands, the program modifications. Considering the lack of separation of duties in the IT environment, which of the following should the information systems (IS) auditor recommend to the IT management to mitigate the risk?

options.A: Automated logging of changes to development libraries
options.B: Additional staff to provide segregation/separation of duties (SoD)
options.C: Procedures that verify that only approved program changes are implemented
options.D: Access controls to prevent the operator from making program modifications

questions.correct_explanation: An information systems (IS) auditor must consider recommending a better process. An IS auditor should recommend a formal change control process that manages and can detect changes to production source and object code, such as code comparisons, so the changes can be reviewed on a regular basis by a third party. This is a compensating control process.

wrong_explanations.A: Logging of changes to production libraries is a good practice, but, because the administrator can alter the logs, this is not a sufficient control.
wrong_explanations.B: Although adherence to segregation/separation of duties (SoD) and recruitment of additional staff are preferred , this practice is not always possible in small enterprises.
wrong_explanations.D: Requiring a third party to do the changes may not be practical in a small enterprise where another person with adequate expertise may not be available.

tips: Independence: an auditor reports and recommends — never fixes, never approves operationally, and never audits work they themselves designed.

questions.question: Which is the MOST important step an auditor should consider while developing an audit plan based on a risk-based approach?

options.A: Inventory the information systems in use in the enterprise and categorize them.
options.B: Assess what risk affect systems and the severity of the impact on the business.
options.C: Determine which systems impact critical enterprise functions and how close to real time they operate.
options.D: Rank the systems based on risk assessment and decide the audit priority, resources, schedule and frequency.

questions.correct_explanation: While planning the audit, the auditor decides what level of audit risk they are willing to accept. The more effective and extensive the audit work is, the less risk of a weakness going undetected. Understanding the critical systems of an enterprise and how close to real time they operate will help ensure that the auditor has the information needed to make a risk decision.

wrong_explanations.A: An inventory alone will not provide sufficient information to assess risk related to critical functions.
wrong_explanations.B: Audit risk is dependent on the auditor's assessed levels of inherent risk (the susceptibility of an audit area to error, which can be material, assuming there are no related internal controls), control risk (the risk a material weakness will not be prevented or detected by internal controls) and detection risk (the risk substantive tests will not detect an error which can be material).
wrong_explanations.D: Not all systems require a place in the audit plan; some noncritical systems may rank higher than critical systems. Critical systems impacting the business should get priority in the audit plan when a risk-based approach is taken.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: What is the MAIN benefit of implementing a risk-based audit? A risk-based audit approach:

options.A: links internal auditing to the enterprise's overall risk management framework.
options.B: ensures that risk, risk responses and actions are being properly classified and reported.
options.C: helps to identify residual risk not in line with the risk appetite, so that appropriate action is being taken to treat the risk.
options.D: allows auditors to provide assurance to the board of directors that risk management processes are managing risk effectively in relation to the risk appetite.

questions.correct_explanation: The main benefit of implementing a risk-based audit is to assure senior management about the efficacy of risk management processes based on the outcome of the audit. Risk management processes, including the effectiveness of responses and the completion of actions, are being monitored by management to ensure that they continue to operate effectively.

wrong_explanations.A: Linking internal audit to the enterprise's overall risk management framework is one benefit derived from implementing risk-based audit, but it is not the main benefit. Risk-based audit refers to the enterprise's risk management framework.
wrong_explanations.B: Classifying and reporting risk, responses and actions is not the main benefit; this is one of the outcomes of the risk-based audit.
wrong_explanations.C: Identifying residual risk not in line with risk appetite is an outcome of the risk-based audit, but not the main benefit.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An IT auditor reviewed the transactions log of an audit engagement partner and discovered some suspicious activity, which may be interpreted as potential fraud. However, the auditor was not able to determine the circumstances around the incidents or obtain further evidence. The auditor decided to disclose this information in case there are questions in the audit quality assurance review. In taking this action, the auditor has:

options.A: violated auditing standards because the auditor should inform the appropriate authorities/management of the suspected fraud.
options.B: violated laws because unlawful activities should have been reported to the appropriate regulatory agency.
options.C: not violated auditing standards because the auditor has committed to disclose the facts, when required.
options.D: not violated auditing standards because there is a Jack of evidence as to whether a fraud has been committed or not.

questions.correct_explanation: In situations where auditors are not able to obtain sufficient or appropriate audit evidence necessary to achieve the audit objectives, they should disclose the situation to audit management and, if necessary, to those charged with audit governance, as per established procedures. Restrictions or limitations on the scope of the audit and achievement of the audit objectives should also be disclosed in the communication of the audit results. The auditor should also inform the appropriate authorities in the enterprise if the indicators of the fraud are sufficient to recommend an investigation. Thus, the auditor has a duty to act even though the available facts do not prove that an irregularity has occurred. Auditors should disclose all material facts and findings known to them that, if not disclosed, may distort the reporting of activities under review.

wrong_explanations.B: Unlawful activities should not be reported to the outside entities until there is sufficient evidence; however, the suspicion of these activities should be disclosed to appropriate executives within the enterprise.
wrong_explanations.C: The auditor has a duty to report the results of audit work in the audit communication.
wrong_explanations.D: Limitations on the achievement of audit objectives should be disclosed in the audit results and reporting, and a possible irregularity should be disclosed to the appropriate enterprise authorities.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.
